business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bioreactor Fermentation and Purification of Biosimilar Antibodies

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition; unitary national legal system with limited custom-based commercial law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between France and the People's Republic of China on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (1984, entered into force 1985)
Convention between France and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income, as amended by the 2013 Protocol

Convention between the United States of America and France for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (signed 1994, as subsequently amended)
Convention between France and India for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1992, as amended)
Convention between France and the Federal Republic of Germany for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1959, as amended)
EU Treaty provisions guaranteeing freedom of establishment (Article 49 TFEU) and free movement of capital (Article 63 TFEU)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 et seq. and L.561-2-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Articles L.123-46-1, L.561-45, L.561-46 et seq. of the Commercial Code jointly implementing the EU 4th, 5th and 6th Anti-Money Laundering Directives; Décret n° 2017-1094 of 6 June 2017 on the beneficial-owner register; Arrêté of 5 July 2019 fixing the model UBO declaration; Loi n° 2016-1691 of 1 December 2016 (Loi Sapin II); EU Directives 2015/849, 2018/843 and 2018/1673 as transposed; Ordinance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial or private-signature Articles of Association of the SAS (Statuts constitutifs) — notarial deed mandatory where the contribution is an immovable asset or registered business contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French notary (notaire), if notarial form applies, or the shareholders under sous-seing privé
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 for any foreign shareholder's signature act; French-origin documents require no legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Capital Deposit Certificate/Blocked Funds Attestation (Attestation de consignation ou de dépôt de fonds)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or a credit institution holding the French bank account of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not subject to apostille or consular legalization; internal banking certification valid vis-à-vis the INPI Guichet Unique

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) filed by the legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: INPI acting as registrar of the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Electronic filing through the Guichet Unique; no apostille required; filing due within 15 days after RCS registration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity, proof-of-address and criminal-record documents of managers and UBOs, including foreign parent-company corporate registers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National registry authorities, police records office (Casier judiciaire national), foreign companies registry or competent municipal authority of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for documents from States party to the 1961 Convention; consular legalization (French Consulate) for non-Hague States; certified translation by a French court-approved translator (traducteur assermenté)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Procuration) authorizing the local incorporator/lawyer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary public or authorized corporate representative of the overseas shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in the country of signature, followed by sworn translation into French

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory compliance with Article L.561-10 (PEP definition), Article L.561-5 (customer due diligence) and Article L.561-15 (enhanced vigilance) of the Code monétaire et financier. The incorporator must screen all shareholders, UBOs, managers and signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, and the French national asset-freezing measures, and apply PEP screening using a FATF-compliant commercial database (e.g., World-Check/Refinitiv, LexisNexis). Hits must be escalated; any freezing order triggers an immediate declaration to TRACFIN and to the Direction générale du Trésor. A suspicious-transaction report (déclaration de soupçon) must be filed with TRACFIN without delay where thresholds of Article L.561-15 are met; records of CDD must be retained 5 years (Article L.561-12).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Entreprises operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; RCS and firm-name availability searched through data.inpi.fr and the infogreffe.fr portal of the commercial court greffes
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS dénomination sociale must be reported in the Articles of Association and inscribed at the RCS in Latin script. Statutory documents are required in French (Article 2 of the French Constitution; Loi Toubon of 4 August 1994); a foreign-language trading name may be used only together with a French version or transliteration and must not create confusion with prior trademark or RCS rights.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France and its derivatives (use of the national designation requires prior administrative authorization)
Assurance, Mutuelle, Organisme de placement collectif, SICAV (regulated financial activities requiring prior authorization)
National, République, Officiel, Agréé (misleading official-status indicators)
Pharmacie, Officine, Laboratoire, Clinique, Hôpital (healthcare-denomination restrictions; prior regulatory qualification or ANSM acknowledgement required)
Avocat, Notaire, Expert-Comptable, Médecin (regulated professional titles reserved to licensed practitioners)
Nobel, Pasteur, Curie (protected names in the scientific sector rising trademark objections)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Guichet Unique or RCS registrar raises a name conflict, the applicant may within the same portal first correct the dossier by substituting a modified name. If the statutory rejection notice is confirmed, the applicant must file a written recours gracieux with INPI within 30 days of the notice; refusal of that recours may be challenged by an appeal for excess of power (recours pour excès de pouvoir) before the Tribunal administratif within two months of the refusal. Parallel trademark/name opposition is decided under Articles L.712-4 to L.712-7 and R.712-14 of the Intellectual Property Code; the INPI opposition decision is appealable to the Paris Cour d'appel. A new name reservation may be lodged immediately without prejudice to the pending appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or domiciliation service may validly hold only the commercial siège social (Article L.123-11-2 of the Commercial Code) and only where the real seat of management and decision-making is verifiable; it cannot be used for the ANSM-licensed pharmaceutical manufacturing establishment under Article L.5124-3 of the Public Health Code, which requires a physical production and quality-control site compliant with EU Good Manufacturing Practice (Directive 2003/94/EC). For a monoclonal-antibody biosimilar manufacturer, virtual office is therefore not permissible for the licensed operating site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Authority: ANSM. Probability of an on-site GMP inspection (announced or unannounced) within 12 months of obtaining the établissement pharmaceutique authorization is assessed at approximately 80%; within 24 months, greater than 90%, including unannounced short-notice inspections of the purified-bulk and sterile-fill areas, consistent with the European Medicines Agency/CIA inspection coordination model for biologics.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI Guichet Unique incorporation filing fee (redevance INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (€54) set by INPI for company registrations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration taxes and greffe formalities (droits de greffe and taxe pour frais de justice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce de Paris or competent commercial court greffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory rate of the national tariff of greffiers (Tarif des greffiers des tribunaux de commerce)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory legal announcement (annonce légale) of the constitution of the SAS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales authorized in the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated market benchmark of approximately €190–€230 for capital-company announcements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of the corporate bank account and block-letter capital deposit attestation (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution (e.g., Bpifrance-cash desk partner, commercial bank)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing bank price list for professional account opening and escrow certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS Articles of Association, Shareholders' Pact annex and corporate record opening (bilingual French/English)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French corporate counsel / notaire in advisory capacity
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for biopharma SAS formation (USD 1,200–2,200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial-owner declaration preparation and electronic RBE filing through the Guichet Unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee portion plus professional fee benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French sworn translation and Hague Apostille/consular legalization of foreign corporate documents, passports and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traducteur assermenté and Ministry of Foreign Affairs-authority or French consulate of the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per certified page plus official apostille/consular tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enhanced PEP, sanctions and adverse-media screening against UN, EU, OFAC and French national lists, with CDD report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a screening file covering all shareholders, UBOs and managers

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) or business center
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (USD 200–300 per month) for the commercial registered office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: ANSM pharmaceutical establishment authorization pre-screening and Stage-2 regulatory readiness review (bridging opinion for ISIC 2100 biosimilar manufacturing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Regulatory affairs and French public-health law counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a pre-filing dossier audit of an établissement pharmaceutique

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. governing the Trade and Companies Register; French Civil Code Articles 1832 et seq. governing companies generally.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent registry is the relevant Registry of Commerce and Companies (Registre du commerce et des sociétés) maintained by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce), with filing submitted through the National Business Formalities Single Window operated by the National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of creation of a legal entity through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, supported by the executed SAS articles of association and the required beneficial ownership declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required; the articles may specify any capital amount, including EUR 1. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash contributions must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations before registration. Contributions in kind must be fully transferred at incorporation, subject to statutory auditor exemptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President records that the SAS has been duly incorporated under its executed articles of association. The Company accepts the subscription of the issued shares by the founders and confirms that the required cash contributions have been deposited and released in accordance with applicable law. The registered office is adopted at the address stated in the articles. The Board appoints [Name] as President and [Name] as Directeur Général, each with the powers specified in the articles and applicable law. The officers are authorized to complete all registrations, banking, tax, employment, regulatory, and licensing formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the registered office and prepare constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises and the selected commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a legally usable registered-office address through ownership evidence, a domiciliation agreement, or a valid lease. Draft the SAS articles in French, identify shareholders, capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, President, and any Directeur Général, and obtain signatures using a legally reliable electronic or handwritten execution process.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and officers
Shareholder declaration of non-conviction and parentage for each individual officer
Corporate authority documents for corporate shareholders
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct address, signature, identification, or authority defects and resubmit through the Guichet unique. Preserve the filing receipt and respond to registry or INPI queries within the stated cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit share capital and document subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account, transfer the subscribed cash capital, obtain the certificate of deposit, and record each shareholder subscription in the capital table. Ensure that at least half of cash contributions is paid before registration and that the articles accurately reflect the subscribed and paid amount.
required_dossiers: Draft or executed articles of association
Shareholder identity and beneficial ownership information
Proof of source of funds where requested under AML procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide corrected KYC, beneficial ownership, source-of-funds, or subscription documents. If the bank declines onboarding, obtain a written refusal and approach another eligible depositary or use the statutory procedure applicable to the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Accredited legal-announcement publication service in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a statutory notice of incorporation containing the SAS name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, President, and registration particulars. Use an authorized publication service and obtain the publication certificate for the registration file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish a corrected notice if mandatory information is inaccurate or omitted, retain both certificates, and attach the corrected publication evidence to the registry submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, electronically routed to the competent commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic creation declaration, upload the articles, capital deposit certificate, publication certificate, registered-office evidence, officer declarations, identity documents, and beneficial ownership information. Confirm the principal activity code and indicate that the business will manufacture biological medicinal products subject to pharmaceutical and environmental authorizations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer electronic deficiency notices through the Guichet unique, replace rejected files in the prescribed format, and correct inconsistent activity, address, capital, or beneficial ownership information before the registry deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration identifiers and activate corporate operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE for SIREN and SIRET identifiers; competent commercial court registry for the Kbis extract; French tax administration for tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the registration extract, verify the legal name, registered office, officers, activity, and registration date, then provide the Kbis and registration identifiers to the bank to release the capital account. Complete VAT, corporate tax, payroll, social-security, and customs registrations as applicable.
required_dossiers: Corporate tax and payroll registration data
Customs or EORI application, if cross-border trade is planned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction from the registry or INSEE where identifiers or published particulars are inaccurate, and file amended corporate information through the Guichet unique when a post-registration change is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt governance records and regulatory delegation controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company records maintained by the SAS; ANSM and other regulators for delegated regulated functions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the statutory register of decisions, shareholder register, share-transfer records, beneficial ownership records, accounting books, and officer appointment documentation. Adopt written delegations for quality, pharmacovigilance, environmental, occupational safety, customs, and AML responsibilities, without exceeding the authority granted by the articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Record corrective resolutions, ratify unauthorized acts where legally permissible, replace defective delegations, and update the registry when an officer, registered office, activity, or beneficial owner changes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: French National Agency for Medicines and Health Products Safety (Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé, ANSM) for pharmaceutical-establishment authorization and the relevant prefecture, assisted by the Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement, DREAL), for classified-installation and environmental approvals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'ouverture d'un établissement pharmaceutique as a manufacturer of medicinal products, including applicable ANSM manufacturing authorization and EU Good Manufacturing Practice compliance; separate Autorisation environnementale, ICPE registration, or ICPE declaration may be required for the physical installation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: French Ministry for Ecological Transition, with the competent DREAL or DRIEAT and the prefecture as the local environmental authorities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Case-dependent. The facility must be screened under the Environmental Code for classified installations for environmental protection (ICPE) and applicable project-assessment rules. Depending on capacity, substances, emissions, storage, and process configuration, the project may require a full environmental impact assessment and environmental authorization, ICPE registration, or ICPE declaration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable prefectural authorization or ICPE order, Water Code requirements, EU Industrial Emissions Directive and BAT conclusions where applicable, and local sewer-discharge permits. Establish validated limits and monitoring for wastewater parameters, biological and chemical oxygen demand, suspended solids, pH, active pharmaceutical ingredients, disinfectants, VOCs, air emissions, odor, hazardous waste, biological waste, and solvent storage. No universal facility-wide thresholds apply without the final ICPE classification and discharge authorization.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire-safety review and operational clearance from the competent prefecture and local fire and rescue service (Service départemental d'incendie et de secours, SDIS), as applicable to the building classification. Complete building-permit and structural-load compliance, hazardous-area and ATEX assessment where relevant, pressure-equipment controls, emergency planning, chemical and biological risk assessments, occupational-health arrangements, and workplace compliance with the Labour Code under the competent DREETS and labour-inspection authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS entities obtain SIREN (9 digits) and SIRET (14 digits) upon incorporation through greffe du tribunal de commerce; VAT identification number is FR followed by SIREN. Foreign-owned entities follow identical incorporation process via French notary or greffe; no separate foreign TIN required for French-resident entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under French tax code; subject to mandatory entity-level corporate taxation. Hybrid mismatch rules governed by ATAD directive without elective treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory facturation électronique for all VAT-registered businesses since 2024; real-time PEP reporting for large taxpayers; digital stamping and API integration with DGFiP platforms required for invoice issuance and clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods to non-EU countries and certain offshore services when export is substantiated by customs declaration, transport documents, and proof of non-EU delivery or service performance outside France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger penalties up to 80% of VAT due plus interest; retrospective clawback of zero-rated amounts with potential criminal prosecution under French tax code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a fully liberalized FX regime under EU law. Capital account transactions (equity investments, loans) are convertible without prior approval. Current account transactions including profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are fully convertible with no surrender obligations. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to tax compliance, beneficial ownership declarations, and AML verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank. Exporters may retain foreign currency proceeds offshore or convert to Euro at prevailing market rates. No statutory conversion ratios apply; repatriation timeline is flexible but all transactions require commercial documentation and reporting if exceeding €10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border operations via Electronic Money Institutions are feasible under French Monetary and Financial Code and PSD2 licensing. Legal constraints include mandatory capital requirements, ongoing AML/KYC obligations, and restrictions on proprietary activities. Overall viability rating: Medium with full regulatory compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding is permitted for French SAS entities using eIDAS-qualified electronic identification. Physical presence is not mandatory for standard KYC but may be required for initial interviews or enhanced due diligence in high-risk or newly incorporated entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declarations, corporate ownership structure, direct and indirect shareholdings, and source of wealth documentation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically exposed persons screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening reports against EU and French sanctions lists, PEP declarations, and adverse media checks
Copies of manufacturing licenses, GMP certifications, export permits, and third-party audit reports for monoclonal antibody production

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are processed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'Capital contribution' or 'Equity injection'. Verification protocols require shareholder resolutions, incorporation certificates, beneficial ownership declarations, and exchange control filings where applicable. All wires must include full beneficiary details and reference codes for audit trails.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit for structured deferred payments. For biopharma exports, LCs are standard for large orders. Clearing involves correspondent banking networks ensuring settlement in target currencies with proper invoicing and destination country import compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit or loss by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing authority; decision recorded in the company's minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court grants an extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A court may compel approval and impose a daily penalty; directors may incur civil liability for failure to convene shareholders or prepare accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit, including the management report where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (greffe) for the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval; two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The president of the commercial court may order filing under a daily penalty. Failure may also result in a civil fine of up to EUR 1,500, or EUR 3,000 for repeat offences; no automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, electronically by the second business day after 1 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% after formal notice and 80% in specified cases, plus late-payment interest; no corporate strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate real estate contribution (CFE) declaration or payment, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is generally payable by 15 December; an initial 1447-C declaration is due by 31 December of the year of creation, and an annual 1447-M declaration is required only for specified changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment generally incurs a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest; no strike-off applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor if it exceeds at least two of these three thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 employees. Separate, including lower, thresholds and rules may apply to groups and entities controlled by or controlling another entity. Biopharmaceutical activity alone does not create a general statutory audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Commercial Code and French generally accepted accounting principles (Plan comptable général). IFRS is required for consolidated accounts of listed groups and may be permitted for certain other consolidated accounts; it does not replace French statutory individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no general annual UBO reconfirmation filing. The company must keep its beneficial ownership information accurate and file an update with the commercial court registry within 30 days after becoming aware of a change. Share transfers must be recorded in the company's securities movement records and individual shareholder accounts; update the UBO filing if the change affects reportable beneficial ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and individual securities accounts, maintained at the registered office or by the authorized account keeper
Minutes and records of shareholder decisions
Accounting records and supporting documents; retain for 10 years
Beneficial ownership information and filed declarations, available to competent authorities

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 200-1,000 annually, approximately USD 220-1,100; provider and location dependent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 5,000-20,000 annually, approximately USD 5,500-22,000; higher for complex or regulated biopharmaceutical operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. A qualifying small enterprise may access a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to French ownership, turnover, capital and fully paid-in capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax losses are generally carried forward without a time limit, but utilization is capped annually at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Loss carryback is generally available for the immediately preceding accounting period, capped at the lower of the preceding period's profit or EUR 1 million. Research and development tax credit is generally 30% of eligible R&D expenditure in metropolitan France up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to eligibility and substantiation. Patent and qualifying intellectual-property income may qualify for a separate 10% rate under the French intellectual-property regime. Certain new businesses, innovation projects and investment zones may benefit from time-limited exemptions or credits subject to statutory conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward period; annual utilization is subject to the EUR 1 million plus 50% excess-profit limitation. The value of 5 years is not the applicable general French rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD: corporate income tax return (impôt sur les sociétés), filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional area using the EFI or EDI procedure. Forms 2050-SD through 2059-G-SD contain the corporate tax package and financial schedules. Form 2572-SD is used for corporate tax balance and installment regularization.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; four corporate tax installments are generally payable during the year, followed by a final balance payment. Monthly payroll-related and withholding filings may apply separately.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and corporate tax balance are generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the statutory filing deadline is generally the second business day after 1 May of the following year. Electronic payment of installments is generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions and first-year rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, legal form, fiscal year dates, principal activity and filing period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS registered details and SIREN. Report the French permanent establishment or subsidiary separately from the foreign shareholder or parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax liability, tax-consolidation status, parent-company status, turnover information and relevant regime elections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify any French tax consolidation group and the designated parent. A non-resident parent does not itself become the French tax filer merely by owning the SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax credits, provisions, depreciation differences, transfer-pricing adjustments and other tax items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-source items that are not attributable to the French company, but include all French taxable income and any related-party adjustments attributable to the SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss, carried-forward losses, loss carryback claim and utilized losses subject to the annual limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not import losses of the foreign parent or an unrelated foreign affiliate. French losses must be supported by French tax returns and statutory accounting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible tax credits, including R&D credit, foreign tax credits where applicable, and other statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain project documentation, invoices, personnel records, technical descriptions and allocation schedules. Foreign parent-funded expenditure is not automatically eligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross and net fixed assets, inventories, receivables, cash, research assets and other assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record assets legally or economically belonging to the SAS. Intercompany receivables, financing balances and capitalized development costs must reconcile to related-party schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, reserves, retained earnings, provisions, debt, trade payables and related-party liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose shareholder loans and foreign-affiliate balances consistently with withholding-tax, thin-capitalization, interest-limitation and transfer-pricing analyses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue, production costs, payroll, depreciation, financial income and expense, exceptional items and net accounting profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue recognition must reflect the manufacturing, licensing, distribution and contract terms for biosimilar antibodies. Related-party revenue must reconcile to invoices, customs records and transfer-pricing policies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation, provisions, personnel costs, subcontracting, royalties, finance charges, exceptional expenses and other deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain evidence for clinical, regulatory, quality-control, manufacturing and R&D expenditure. Royalty and service charges require benefit evidence, contractual support and arm's-length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions with associated enterprises, transfer-pricing information and foreign related-party dealings where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report material cross-border controlled transactions, including goods, technology, royalties, services, financing, guarantees and cost-sharing arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax balance after crediting installments and applicable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay electronically from the SAS's French tax account. A foreign shareholder cannot substitute its own tax payment for the SAS's French liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: 2067-SD, excess interest and related-party expense disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information on certain interest, commissions and payments to related parties or persons receiving preferential tax treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review shareholder, treasury and group-financing arrangements, including guarantees and debt issued by foreign affiliates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file generally attracts a 10% surcharge, potentially increased in cases involving formal notice or abusive conduct. Late payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Inaccurate returns may attract penalties generally ranging from 40% for deliberate non-compliance to 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive-law situations. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a penalty generally equal to the higher of EUR 50,000 or 0.5% of the transactions covered by the missing documentation, subject to statutory calculation rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD and tax package transmitted through impots.gouv.fr professional EDI or EFI filing systems; Form 2035 or VAT forms are not substitutes for the SAS corporate tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly VAT or monthly VAT depending on the applicable VAT regime; annual VAT return may apply to qualifying taxpayers under the simplified regime. VAT compliance is separate from corporate income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: VAT deadlines depend on the chosen regime, taxable turnover and tax authority instructions. Monthly VAT returns are generally due during the following month; annual simplified-regime returns and installment forms follow the statutory timetable shown in the professional tax account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Output VAT, domestic taxable supplies, intra-Community supplies, exports and reverse-charge transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify biosimilar antibody sales by destination, Incoterms, customs status, customer VAT number and place-of-supply rules. Exports require customs evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Input VAT on qualifying purchases, capital equipment, subcontracting, logistics and operating costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain valid French invoices and import VAT documentation. Foreign supplier invoices may require reverse-charge treatment rather than direct deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CA3, reverse charge and intra-Community fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: VAT due on imported services, intra-Community acquisitions and other reverse-charge transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review foreign group services, licensing, contract manufacturing and logistics charges for French reverse-charge VAT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: VAT late filing or payment generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased where formal notice or fraudulent conduct is involved, plus late-payment interest. Inaccurate VAT returns may generate additional penalties and denial of input-tax recovery.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident recipient, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption, implemented in French law, may reduce withholding to 0% where the parent satisfies qualifying legal-form, tax-subject-to-tax, minimum ownership, holding-period and anti-abuse conditions. French resident individual recipients are generally subject to a 12.8% income-tax withholding component, in addition to social levies where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain and retain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's competent foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, and apply the applicable treaty rate only where French procedural requirements are satisfied. Use the relevant French tax-residence and treaty forms, including Form 5000 and the applicable dividend form, where required. If relief cannot be established at source, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund claim with supporting residence, ownership, payment and beneficial-owner evidence. Anti-abuse, principal-purpose, conduit and beneficial-ownership rules must be reviewed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents may generally be subject to a 25% withholding tax under Article 182 B of the French Tax Code, subject to treaty reduction, EU interest-and-royalties relief and qualifying intellectual-property regimes. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, except for specific categories, anti-abuse situations and payments involving non-cooperative jurisdictions or other statutory exceptions. Treaty rates vary by recipient state and treaty article; treaty entitlement must be confirmed transaction by transaction. Payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions may face elevated withholding, including rates up to 75% for specified income categories.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer-pricing documentation under Article L13 AA generally applies where French turnover or gross assets is at least EUR 150 million, or where the company controls, is controlled by, or belongs to a group involving an entity meeting the statutory threshold. Simplified documentation may apply below that threshold where the French entity engages in material controlled transactions, including transactions meeting the applicable EUR 50 million statutory threshold. A country-by-country report generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Intercompany transactions remain arm's-length and supportable even below documentation thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single standalone economic-substance-regulation regime equivalent to certain jurisdiction-specific ESR statutes. Substance is nevertheless enforced through the abuse-of-law doctrine, principal-purpose and treaty anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled-foreign-company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation, general anti-abuse principles and transfer-pricing provisions. The SAS should maintain French decision-making, qualified personnel, suitable premises, manufacturing and quality systems, risk control, board records, financial capacity and genuine commercial functions proportionate to its claimed profits. A French company that is contractually characterized as a routine manufacturer but bears no operational risks must not retain residual entrepreneurial returns without factual support.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent corporate tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating expenses, misclassifying shareholder distributions, manipulating inventory or development costs, or deliberately understating French taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest and penalties generally up to 80% in the most serious cases. Tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases carrying imprisonment of up to 7 years and a fine of up to EUR 3 million or twice the proceeds, subject to applicable law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur criminal liability, civil tax liability for fraudulent or repeated non-compliance, asset-preservation measures and management bans. Courts may impose travel restrictions or detention-related measures where justified in criminal proceedings; imprisonment is not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and undocumented related-party dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting antibody manufacturing profit through unsupported royalties, procurement charges, management fees, financing costs, contract-manufacturing remuneration or intellectual-property allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to arm's-length profit, interest and penalties. Missing or materially incomplete documentation may trigger a specific penalty generally equal to the higher of EUR 50,000 or 0.5% of the transactions covered by the missing documentation, subject to statutory rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for deliberate misstatements, fraudulent accounting, insolvency-related misconduct and tax-fraud participation. Corporate protection does not shield personal criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend, royalty and interest withholding failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying foreign affiliates without withholding, applying treaty relief without residence or beneficial-owner evidence, or disguising distributions as royalties, services or loan interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, late-payment interest, tax penalties and possible denial of treaty relief. Repeated or fraudulent withholding violations may create criminal exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be pursued for intentional withholding failures, fraudulent distributions and breaches of tax-payment duties. Personal liability depends on conduct, fault and insolvency circumstances.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty shopping and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a nominal French SAS with no personnel, premises, decision-making, manufacturing capacity or commercial risk while routing profits, dividends, royalties or financing through it solely to obtain tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or statutory benefits, recharacterization of transactions, corporate tax reassessment, withholding-tax recovery, abuse-of-law penalties and possible criminal tax-fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face criminal liability for participation in fraudulent arrangements, asset confiscation, management bans and civil claims for losses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misstating origin, tariff classification, customs value, export status or destination of biological products; claiming unsupported zero-rating; or deducting input VAT on fictitious or non-business invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs duties, import VAT, VAT reassessment, interest, penalties, seizure, loss of customs authorizations and potential criminal prosecution for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, customs representatives and responsible officers may face personal criminal liability, fines, confiscation and professional or management restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manufacturing or distributing monoclonal antibodies or biosimilars without required authorization, Good Manufacturing Practice compliance, batch-release controls, pharmacovigilance systems, qualified-person oversight or traceability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative suspension or withdrawal of authorization, product recall, seizure, fines, civil product liability and criminal sanctions under French public-health law. Tax deductions and R&D-credit claims may also be challenged where expenditure is unlawful or unsupported.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and qualified persons may face criminal prosecution, professional sanctions, civil damages and, in serious cases, imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained funds, concealing beneficial ownership, using opaque intermediaries, failing customer and supplier due diligence, or not reporting suspicious transactions through the applicable French AML channels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fines, transaction restrictions, confiscation and criminal sanctions for money laundering or terrorist financing. Money laundering may carry imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 375,000, with aggravated cases carrying higher penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally prosecuted for knowing participation, facilitation or deliberate failure to maintain mandatory controls. Assets may be frozen or confiscated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining inaccurate statutory accounts, recording fictitious liabilities, distributing profits without distributable reserves, or disguising shareholder withdrawals as business expenditure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Account restatement, tax reassessment, repayment of unlawful distributions, fines, director disqualification and criminal sanctions under French company law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unlawful distributions, misuse of corporate assets, presentation of misleading accounts, insolvency misconduct and creditor losses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming research credit for routine quality-control, regulatory, commercial, manufacturing or duplicated group work without qualifying scientific uncertainty and contemporaneous technical evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of the tax credit, interest, penalties, denial of future claims and possible audit referral. Deliberate fabrication may constitute tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and technical signatories may face civil and criminal exposure for knowingly false claims, fabricated records or coordinated fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing ultimate owners, dealing with sanctioned persons or jurisdictions, exporting controlled biological materials without authorization, or using intermediaries to bypass EU or French restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transaction blocking, asset freezing, administrative fines, confiscation, loss of licenses and criminal prosecution under sanctions, customs and export-control laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance personnel may face personal fines, imprisonment, confiscation and management prohibitions for knowing or reckless violations.
